It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}, and under the former {{ill|Q712534|lt=shrine ranking}} it was a {{ill|Fu-sha|qid=Q134917326|lt=Fusha}}. It is the {{ill|Izumi Province|Q1047117|qid=Q1047117}}{{ill|Ichinomiya|Q1656379|qid=Q1656379|lt=Sannomiya}}. It is also called “Shinoda Myōjin,” “Shinoda-sha,” and “Shinoda Hijiri-sha.” {{nihongo|'''Hijiri Shrine'''|聖神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Izumi Province]].

== Enshrined deity ==
* Hijiri Ōkami (ひじりのおおかみ)
Hijiri Ōkami is a {{ill|Mikogami|de|Mikokami|ja|御子神|zh|御子神|qid=Q352176}} of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ōtoshi no Kami}}, who appears as “Hijiri no Kami” in the '{{ill|Kojiki|Q813031|qid=Q813031}}.' According to the 'Izumi no Kuni Ōtori Gosha Daimyōjin narabi ni Fuchū Sōsha Hachimangū Engi,' its {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=honji-butsu}} is {{ill|Kṣitigarbha|Q604687|qid=Q604687}}.

{{要出典範囲|According to shrine-family tradition, the following five deities are said to be enshrined. They are apparently now accompanying deities.|date=March 2010}}.
* {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|Q1056017|qid=Q1056017|lt=Ninigi-no-Mikoto}}
* {{ill|Amaterasu|Q455602|qid=Q455602}}
* {{ill|Nigihayahi|Q10949054|qid=Q10949054|lt=Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto}}
* {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|Q1781862|qid=Q1781862|lt=Konohanasakuya-hime-no-Mikoto}}
* {{ill|Iwanaga-hime|Q8191705|qid=Q8191705|lt=Iwanaga-hime-no-Mikoto}}

Obito, an immigrant {{ill|Clan|Q211503|qid=Q211503}} of {{ill|Toraijin|Q11561926|qid=Q11561926|lt=continental origin}}, enshrined Hijiri Ōkami. On May 7, {{ill|Jōgan|Q1075635|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jōgan}} 1 ({{ill|859|Q23897|qid=Q23897}}), it was designated a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kansha}}, and on August 13 of the same year received {{ill|Shinkai (divine rank)|Q11591025|qid=Q11591025}} advancement from Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade to Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade ('{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|qid=Q1052981|lt=Sandai Jitsuroku}}'). In the '{{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}' enforced in {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Enchō}} 5 ({{ill|927|ab|927|af|927|am|927 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|927|ar|927|ary|927|ast|927|avk|927|az|927|azb|۹۲۷ (میلادی)|bar|927|bcl|927|be|927|be_x_old|927|bg|927|bn|৯২৭|bpy|মারি ৯২৭|br|927|bs|927.|ca|927|cdo|927 nièng|ceb|927|ckb|٩٢٧|crh|927|cs|927|csb|927|cv|927|cy|927|da|927|de|927|el|927|eml|927|eo|927|es|927|et|927|eu|927|fa|۹۲۷ (میلادی)|fi|927|fo|927|fr|927|fy|927|ga|927|gan|927年|gd|927|gl|927|he|927|hi|927|hr|927.|ht|927 (almanak jilyen)|hu|927|hy|927|id|927|ilo|927|io|927|is|927|it|927|ja|927年|jv|927|ka|927|kaa|927|kk|927 жыл|ko|927년|la|927|lb|927|lij|927|lmo|927|lt|927 m.|lv|927. gads|map_bms|927|mdf|927|mg|927|mhr|927|mi|927|mk|927|mr|इ.स. ९२७|mrj|927 и|ms|927|mzn|۹۲۷|nah|927|nap|927|nds|927|new|सन् ९२७|nl|927|nn|927|no|927|nrm|927|nso|927|oc|927|or|୯୨୭|os|927-æм аз|pl|927|pnb|927|pt|927|qu|927|ro|927|ru|927 год|rue|927|sa|९२७|scn|927|sd|927ع|se|927|sh|927.|shn|927|si|927|sk|927|smn|927|sq|927|sr|927|su|927|sv|927|sw|927|tg|Соли 927|th|พ.ศ. 1470|tk|927|tl|927|tly|927|tr|927|tt|927 ел|uk|927|ur|927ء|uz|927|vec|927|vi|927|war|927|wuu|927年|xmf|927|zh|927年|zh_min_nan|927 nî|zh_yue|927年|qid=Q30470}}), it is listed in the '{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932|lt=Register of Deities}}' ({{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}). In the medieval '{{ill|Izumi Province Divine Name Register|Q11420490|qid=Q11420490|lt=Izumi no Kuni Jinmyōchō}},' its deity rank is “Senior First Rank.”

In the {{ill|Kamakura period|Q236205|qid=Q236205}}, the Shinoda clan served successively as chief priests, but because they sided with the {{ill|Southern Court|Q3001082|qid=Q3001082|lt=Southern Court}} in the {{ill|Nanboku-chō period|Q264012|qid=Q264012|lt=Northern and Southern Courts period}}, they later lost that position, and in {{ill|Enbun|Q1145071|qid=Q1145071}} 5 ({{ill|1360|Q6150|qid=Q6150}}), Wada Kurando became chief priest. From the Nanboku-chō period, together with {{ill|Ōtori taisha|Q705151|qid=Q705151|lt=Ōtori Shrine}}, {{ill|Izumianashi Shrine|Q11554908|qid=Q11554908}}, {{ill|Tsugawa Shrine|Q11597137|qid=Q11597137}}, and {{ill|Hine Shrine|Q11509543|qid=Q11509543}} in the same {{ill|Izumi Province|Q1047117|qid=Q1047117}}, it came to be called one of the “Five Great Deity Shrines.” It held the third rank among shrines of Izumi Province, though the designation “Sannomiya” does not appear in medieval records.

In {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Q1145058|qid=Q1145058}} 3 ({{ill|1575|Q6688|qid=Q6688}}), {{ill|Oda Nobunaga|Q171411|qid=Q171411}} confirmed holdings of 1,100 {{ill|Koku|Q855048|qid=Q855048}}, but in year 13 ({{ill|1585|Q6736|qid=Q6736}}), during {{ill|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|Q187550|qid=Q187550}}’s {{ill|Battle of Kishuu|Q10855721|qid=Q10855721|lt=attack on Negoro}}, it suffered war fire and its lands were confiscated.

In the early {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}}, {{ill|Toyotomi Hideyori|be|Таётомі Хідэёры|ca|Toyotomi Hideyori|cs|Hidejori Tojotomi|de|Toyotomi Hideyori|el|Τογιοτόμι Χιντεγιόρι|eo|Toyotomi Hideyori|es|Toyotomi Hideyori|eu|Toyotomi Hideyori|fa|تویوتومی هیده‌یوری|fi|Toyotomi Hideyori|fr|Toyotomi Hideyori|id|Toyotomi Hideyori|it|Toyotomi Hideyori|ja|豊臣秀頼|ko|도요토미 히데요리|la|Fideyorus|lt|Tojotomi Hidejori|ms|Toyotomi Hideyori|nl|Toyotomi Hideyori|no|Toyotomi Hideyori|pl|Hideyori Toyotomi|pt|Toyotomi Hideyori|ru|Тоётоми Хидэёри|sk|Hidejori Tojotomi|sr|Тојотоми Хидејори|th|โทโยโตมิ ฮิเดโยริ|tr|Toyotomi Hideyori|uk|Тойотомі Хідейорі|vi|Toyotomi Hideyori|zh|豐臣秀賴|qid=Q313641}} had {{ill|Katagiri Katsumoto|Q1882775|qid=Q1882775}} supervise construction of shrines and temples in various places, and this shrine was also rebuilt in {{ill|Keichō|Q1328185|qid=Q1328185}} 9 ({{ill|1604|Q6738|qid=Q6738}}). Existing buildings from that time are the main sanctuary of the main shrine and the sanctuaries of the subsidiary Sansha, Taki Shrine, and Hiraoka Shrine; they are designated {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Q1188622|qid=Q1188622}} and tangible cultural properties of {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ace|Prefektur Osaka|af|Osaka-prefektuur|an|Prefectura d'Osaka|ang|Ōsacascir|ar|أوساكا There was also Manshō-in of the {{ill|Shingon Buddhism|Q550182|qid=Q550182}} as its {{ill|Jingū-ji|Q1074971|qid=Q1074971}}, with a {{ill|Five-storied pagoda|ja|五重塔|ko|오층탑|zh|五重塔|qid=Q11372713}} and bell tower. In {{ill|Kansei|Q1195131|qid=Q1195131}} 8 ({{ill|1796|Q7818|qid=Q7818}}), a dispute occurred between the {{ill|Shake (social class)|Q11588367|qid=Q11588367}} and shrine monks.

In {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}}, due to the {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|ca|Shinbutsu bunri|de|Shinbutsu-Bunri|es|Shinbutsu bunri|fa|شینبوتسو بونری|fi|Shinbutsu bunri|fr|Shinbutsu bunri|id|Shinbutsu bunri|it|Shinbutsu bunri|ja|神仏分離|ru|Симбуцу бунри|tr|Şinbutsu-bunri|zh|神佛分離|qid=Q1970535}}, Manshō-in was abolished. In {{ill|1872|Q7753|qid=Q7753}} (Meiji 5), it was ranked as a village shrine, and in March {{ill|1943|Q18623|qid=Q18623}} ({{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}} 18), it was promoted to {{ill|Fu-sha|qid=Q134917326|lt=Fusha}}.

The “Naka-Izumi Kaidō” extending from Sukematsu-chō, {{ill|Izumiōtsu|Q873553|qid=Q873553}}, is also called the “Nubiki Road,” derived from the tradition that Shinoda Daimyōjin, after landing at Sukematsu-hama, pulled cloth while heading to Hijiri Shrine. A monument for the “Naka-Izumi Kaidō” stands at the intersection with the {{ill|Kishū Kaidō|Q11605050|qid=Q11605050}}.

* Main sanctuary ({{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Q1188622|qid=Q1188622}}) - Rebuilt in {{ill|Keichō|Q1328185|qid=Q1328185}} 9 ({{ill|1604|Q6738|qid=Q6738}}) with {{ill|Toyotomi Hideyori|be|Таётомі Хідэёры|ca|Toyotomi Hideyori|cs|Hidejori Tojotomi|de|Toyotomi Hideyori|el|Τογιοτόμι Χιντεγιόρι|eo|Toyotomi Hideyori|es|Toyotomi Hideyori|eu|Toyotomi Hideyori|fa|تویوتومی هیده‌یوری|fi|Toyotomi Hideyori|fr|Toyotomi Hideyori|id|Toyotomi Hideyori|it|Toyotomi Hideyori|ja|豊臣秀頼|ko|도요토미 히데요리|la|Fideyorus|lt|Tojotomi Hidejori|ms|Toyotomi Hideyori|nl|Toyotomi Hideyori|no|Toyotomi Hideyori|pl|Hideyori Toyotomi|pt|Toyotomi Hideyori|ru|Тоётоми Хидэёри|sk|Hidejori Tojotomi|sr|Тојотоми Хидејори|th|โทโยโตมิ ฮิเดโยริ|tr|Toyotomi Hideyori|uk|Тойотомі Хідейорі|vi|Toyotomi Hideyori|zh|豐臣秀賴|qid=Q313641}} and {{ill|Katagiri Katsumoto|Q1882775|qid=Q1882775}} as magistrate. A shrine building of {{ill|East Asian hip-and-gable roof|Q855025|qid=Q855025}} with {{ill|cypress bark roof|Q90373477|qid=Q90373477}}, 3 bays front and 3 bays depth, decorated on the front with a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=chidori-hafu}}, and with a 1-bay projecting porch ({{ill|kōhai|Q11415970|qid=Q11415970}}) with {{ill|Karahafu|Q977293|qid=Q977293}} eaves. Designated a specially protected structure on April 15, {{ill|1924|Q2173|qid=Q2173}} ({{ill|Taishō era|Q329174|qid=Q329174}} 13) under the {{ill|Ancient Temples and Shrines Preservation Law|Q11411552|qid=Q11411552}}, and became an Important Cultural Property under enforcement of the {{ill|Cultural Properties Protection Law|Q1188502|qid=Q1188502}} in {{ill|1950|Q18597|qid=Q18597}} ({{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}} 25).
* Haiden
* Shrine office
* Hijiri {{ill|Acala|Q337624|qid=Q337624}} - a remnant of {{ill|Shinbutsu-shūgō|Q2279088|qid=Q2279088}}.
* Worship-from-afar site - for {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|Q687168|qid=Q687168}}. Built in modern times.

== Affiliated and subsidiary shrines ==
* Sansha Shrine (Important Cultural Property) - Rebuilt in Keichō 9 (1604) with Toyotomi Hideyori and Katagiri Katsumoto as magistrate. Its polychrome decoration and ornate styling show features of the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Momoyama period}}. The shrine building is a three-bay {{ill|Kasuga-zukuri|Q3193781|qid=Q3193781}} with cypress-bark roof. A three-bay Kasuga-zukuri (three front pillar intervals) is rare nationwide. Relocated to current site in {{ill|1873|Q7757|qid=Q7757}} (Meiji 6).
* Taki Shrine (Important Cultural Property) - Rebuilt in Keichō 9 (1604) with Toyotomi Hideyori and Katagiri Katsumoto as magistrate. Building is one-bay Kasuga-zukuri with cypress-bark roof. Kōhai is made with karahafu eaves. Relocated to current site in 1873 (Meiji 6).
* Hiraoka Shrine (Osaka Prefecture-designated {{ill|Tangible Cultural Property (Japan)|Q2901860|qid=Q2901860}}) - Rebuilt in Keichō 9 (1604) with Toyotomi Hideyori and Katagiri Katsumoto as magistrate. Main sanctuary is one-bay Kasuga-zukuri with cypress-bark roof.
* Kotohira Shrine - Deity: {{ill|Ōmononushi|lt=Ōmononushi|Q10936701|qid=Q10936701}}-no-Kami
* Itsukushima Shrine - Deity: {{ill|Ichikishima-hime|fr|Ichikishimahime|ja|イチキシマヒメ|simple|Ichikishima-hime|zh|市寸島比賣命|qid=Q11059454|lt=Ichikishimahime-no-Mikoto}}
* Inari mounds - There are many Inari mounds enshrining {{ill|Inari Ōkami|Q719665|qid=Q719665}}.
